entries.title: This Completely Changes the Way We Build Production AI Agents (Vercel Eve)
entries.description:
Vercel just open sourced their new AI agent framework Eve, and now your entire production AI agent can be just a single folder of mostly markdown. Instructions are markdown, tools are TypeScript, skills and subagents are just nested folders. Eve compiles the whole thing into a durable service you deploy with one command. Durable execution, an isolated sandbox, human approvals, and evals all ship in the box.

entries.title: I Turned Claude Code Into a Complete Video Generation System (with Archon)
entries.description:
Try Higgsfield: https://higgsfield.ai/s/mcp-colemedin-eChXUF

I turned Claude Code into an AI marketing factory. The whole point of this video is that the tools I use every day for AI coding - Claude Code and Archon - are not limited to coding. Here I aim that exact same setup at a product catalog and let it produce a batch of finished, human-approved video ads on its own along with the help of Higgsfield.

The biggest takeaway is that a coding harness can be used for a lot more than just coding

entries.title: Pydantic AI 2.0: The New Best Way to Build AI Agents is Composing Capabilities
entries.description:
The new best way to build AI agents is to compose capabilities, instead of every agent being a unorganized pile of tools, instructions, and guardrails. That is the shift in Pydantic AI 2.0, and it changes how you build every agent.

A capability is a self-contained brick that bundles its own instructions, tools, model settings, and hooks. You compose an agent by snapping bricks together, and the same brick drops into any other agent unchanged.

entries.title: I Love the Karpathy LLM Wiki but it Doesn't Scale. Here's What Does.
entries.description:
Markdown makes great memory for an AI agent - a Karpathy-style LLM wiki, an Obsidian second brain it reads and writes. If the agent is just yours, a folder of markdown is hard to beat: simple, yours, all in git. My second brain is exactly that!

entries.description:

entries.description:

entries.title: My AI Memory Now Follows Me Across Every Tool!
entries.description:
Your AI agent's memory is trapped inside one tool. The second you switch from Claude Code to Codex or Pi, all that context is gone - and recently I've been switching constantly!

So I started using Walrus Memory: a memory layer that lives outside any single agent, encrypted and owned by you. entries.title: The Creators of Claude Code and OpenClaw don't Prompt Their Agents Anymore?!

entries.title: Omnigent: The New Meta-Harness for EVERY Coding Agent - Claude Code, Codex, Pi, More
entries.description:
The way the best engineers use AI is shifting fast. Instead of committing to a single provider, they use the right model for each job - like using Claude for implementation, and Codex for reviewing, and Kimi/Minimax for simple tasks. The piece we have been missing is a clean way to orchestrate all of those models together. entries.title: Google's Agents CLI: The CLI + Skills Combination to Ship AI Agents EASILY
entries.description:
Building an AI agent is easy these days. The wild part is that shipping one to production is finally just as easy too.
